title: Nolan Wells would have turned 19 Wednesday. Read the birthday letter his family never imagined writing | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Nolan Wells should have turned 19 Wednesday surrounded by a birthday cake, candles and laughter. Instead, the day became one of remembrance for his family, who shared a heartfelt message with CNN to their “Nono” in heaven.

As the family faced the day without Nolan, grief, sorrow and uncertainty loomed as loved ones wrestled with theteen’s unexplained deathlast month during a July 4 boating trip with a group of friends to Mississippi’s Horn Island.

More than six weeks later, authorities are still investigating and have given no public indication that a crime occurred. The unanswered questions have divided communities, left loved ones heartbroken and fueled speculation,harassment and threatsdirected at both Nolan’s familyand the friendswho were with him on the holiday trip.

With his birthday approaching, the unanswered questions compounded his mother Christine Wonsley’s grief as she prepared to celebrate without him.

The“only thing we wanna know is what happened,” she said during a news conference last week. “That’s all we want to know is what happened to our son.”

In a moving letter shared with CNN and later posted on social media, Nolan’s family thanked their “sonshine” for the love and legacy he left behind:

“Today you are 19 Nono! There are so many things we want to say but we will keep it simple. As we sit here and reflect on what an amazing kiddo you grew up to be, we can’t help but to feel blessed, honored, proud, but most of all thankful. Thankful we were able to experience a glimpse of God’s love in human form. Although you are no longer physically here with us, we will always celebrate you and the legacy you have left for us to protect. You have taught us so much about life and how everyday is a blessing and how we have to do better at just living in the moment. Thank you for being the best son, brother, grandson, nephew, and friend anyone could ever ask for. Thank you for bringing joy, laughter and real happiness to us each and every day. You are truly our angel. You will be missed every second of everyday and you will never be forgotten our sweet sonshine 🩵. Happy Heavenly 19th Birthday Nono. Remember don’t eat too much Oreo cake and hug Grandma for us. Mahal na mahal ka namin, aming pinakamamahal na anak at kapatid. (Taglog to English translation: We love you our beloved son and brother) Love, Mom, Dad, Siblings, and Family 🩵”

Loved ones held a national prayer rally Wednesday evening in Nolan’s memory at Greater St. John AME Church in Biloxi, about 5 miles from his hometown of Ocean Springs.

Nolan’s framed sports jerseys were displayed at the front of the church, just below the pulpit where speakers addressed attendees.

At one point during the ceremony, which was streamed online, family members gathered on stage to sing “Happy Birthday” as gold helium balloons shaped like a 1 and 9 hovered over a cake with lit candles.

Dr. Jamal Bryant, senior pastor of New Birth Missionary Baptist Church in Georgia,delivered a keynoteat the event. Those in attendance included Nolan’s family, local elected officials and filmmaker Spike Lee, who previously showed support for the family by attending the teen’s funeral.

“Prayer is a weapon that never runs out of ammunition,” Bryant wrote on Instagram ahead of the event. “Let’s stand with this family and before GOD! This is not over!!”

Civil rights and Wells family attorney Ben Crump echoed the call for solidarity, especially on Nolan’s birthday.

“Can we pray together in unity to say, let’s get to the truth of what happened to Nolan Wells,” Crump said during a news conference last week. “Can we do that, America? Can we at least come together in unity on his birthday?”

The Rev. Al Sharpton and the National Action Networkorganized anationwide virtual prayer vigilWednesday afternoon.

More than 550 people joined Sharpton and Crump online to pray for and reflect with the Wells family while calling for answers about the teen’s death.

Nolan’s father, Elmore Wonsley, said his son would have been in school Wednesday and likely would have called to tell him about his day. Hearing his son’s voice, he said, is one of the things he’ll miss most.

“Just keep us in your prayers, keep us in your thoughts, and we thank every one of you guys for everything that you guys have been doing,” Christine Wonsley, Nolan’s mother, said emotionally during the prayer vigil, urging attendees to keep sharing her son’s story.

An attorney for three of Nolan’s friends who were with him on that boating trip - Warren Hudson, 19; Jax Pitalo, 20; and Morgan Seymour, 19 - posted a tribute for the teen’s birthday on behalf of his clients, saying “just like every day, we honor and remember our dear friend, Nolan Wells.”

“He was the brightest of lights who touched many lives, including ours,” the statement continued. “His memory will shine on in our hearts. Always.”

On July 4, Nolan and a group of friends boarded boats and set out from Ocean Springs to celebrate America’s Independence Day on nearby Horn Island. Nolan’s friends returned after the outing, but he didn’t.

Nearly an hour after Nolan was last seen, friends on one of the boats noticed its bilge pump had failed and water was rapidly filling the hull,Tyler Cox and Edward Paltzik, attorneys for the friends, told CNN. The young men made an emergency call for towing assistance and were focused on dealing with the sinking boat and leaving the island.

Cox disputed claims Wells was left stranded when his clients, Hudson, Pitalo and Seymour, left the area.

“That’s just how it is here. You can always find another ride off the island, and again, there were 2,000 other people there, so he wasn’t left alone by any means,” Cox said.

“They left the island at 4:30 pm … So, we don’t know what happened to Nolan after 4:30,” he said. “We want to know just as much as anybody.”

In the days immediately after the holiday, a frantic search for Nolan ensued, with authorities, friends and family deploying resources to find the missing teen. OnJuly 6, the search ended in heartbreak with the news Nolan’s loved ones had feared the most: a body matching his physical description was recovered from the water near the shoreline, officials said.

Questions have surfaced about why Nolan’s friends had his phone. But Coxtold CNN it’s commonpractice to drop anchor 50 feet offshore and swim to the island, leaving cell phones behind rather than risking saltwater damage to their electronic devices.

Two autopsies have been conducted, but neither have yielded a definitive public explanation for Nolan’s manner of death. An autopsy commissioned by the Wells family wasruled inconclusiveciting a lack of evidence, while the state’s autopsy report is sealed pending review by a grand jury.

The results of the state’s toxicology tests – which are standard in death investigations and can take weeks – are also completed but those findings have not been made public.

Public updates from authorities have been sparse, with investigators referring questions to the district attorney, who said evidence is being reviewed before presenting the case to a grand jury, who will ultimately decide if any crime may have taken place.

In a new statement released Tuesday, Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said she doesn’t have “the same freedom to share information publicly that private individuals may have.”

Wells, she said, deserves better than “stepping outside the bounds of the law” to share information that remains key to the case.

“There is nothing more to be shared at this time. I caution the public about assigning trustworthiness to things they read and see online,” said McIlrath.

While currents around Horn Island can be dangerous even for experienced swimmers, Crump has disputed the theory that Nolan accidentally drowned, saying he was astrong athleteand swimmer.

Last week, the Congressional Black Caucus called on the FBI to launch an independent investigation into Nolan’s death, arguing that federal involvement could give additional scrutiny as key questions about the case loom.

In the weeks since Nolan’s unexplained death, a photo of the Black teen smiling wide, surrounded by White friends, with his arm casually slung around their shoulders while on the holiday boating excursion to Horn Island, has turned a memory among friends into a subject of great conjecture.

In the absence of clear answers from the investigation, strangers across the country have filled the void with competing narratives, particularly about whether race played a role in his death against the backdrop of Mississippi’s fraught racial history.

Some of Wells’ friends who were with him that day and local officials have said they receivedthreats against their lives. Some of the alleged threats were deemed serious enough thatthree people were chargedwith crimes, The Associated Press reported. The suspects, who live in three states outside Mississippi, do not appear to have any connection to the families there.

Hudson, Pitalo, and Seymour have effectively become pariahs in their hometown and have been subjected to death threats and defamation, their attorneys said – some haven’t been able to return to school, and others have been refused service in their town. All three have been questioned by authorities in the case, Cox said.

Meanwhile, Nolan’s father, Elmore Wonsley said his grieving family has also received online attacks — including a sudden barrage of negative reviews against his wife, a nurse practitioner, and vitriol from strangers.

“The disrespect that’s been coming toward my wife and my family — for any parent, no matter what race you are, they need time to grieve,” Elmore Wonsley said at a news conference last month. “A parent can’t grieve when you have people attacking them, attacking their jobs, attacking their character.”

The investigation could move forward with a forensic review of Nolan’s cell phone. The family’s attorneys said their experts are prepared to conduct a joint examination with law enforcement as early as this week.

CNN’s Chelsea Bailey and Holly Yan contributed to this report.

CNN’s Chelsea Bailey and Holly Yan contributed to this report.
